newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods hold steady, buyers snub Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods hold steady, buyers snub Iraq.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices held steady early despite sharp gains in Wednesday's futures markets, which rose on news of fresh tensions between the U.S. and Iraq.
"I have no anxious buyers," one dealer said. "The Merc's up but everyone says who cares...Iraq's been factored in."
Unleaded gasoline for October delivery rose nearly two cents on NYMEX to 66.70 cents a gallon.
Conventional grade gasoline in Los Angeles edged up one cent on the strength in futures, reaching 71.50/72 cents a gallon at midday. Premium held at seven cent advantage.
CARB gasoline was even with Tuesday levels at 72.50/73.50 cents a gallon.
Traders assessed CARB diesel fuel in Los Angeles at 77.50/79 cents a gallon, flat from Tuesday.
Values for jet fuel were notionally flat at 78.50/80 cents after rising two cents early Tuesday.
One trader said jet fuel and distillate were poised to rise further on tensions in Iraq, which could increase the U.S. military's consumption of jet fuel
But today, low sulphur diesel held at 72/73 cents after climbing one cent Tuesday.
San Francisco distillates were the same price as L.A. material.
Bay area CARB grade gasolines stayed three cents cheaper but conventional were pegged notionally a half cent under.
